predecessors.name: Mali Empire
predecessors.text: Gao and the Niger bend around it, which Mali held 'until the 1430s'

successors.name: Saadi Sultanate
successors.text: Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné, the three cities Judar Pasha sacked

successors.name: Dendi Kingdom
successors.text: Dendi, the easternmost province on the Niger under the Dendi-fari, with its fleet at Ayorou; Cliopatria's Songhai shapes stop at 1.7 E and omit it

ledger.x: c. 1435: Gao leaves the Mali Empire and Songhai begins its rise. Infobox 'Independence from Mali Empire: c. 1430s'; the lead puts a Songhai state at Gao 'since the 11th century'. 1435 is a mid-decade year chosen to match the mali-empire dossier.
1464: Sunni Ali inherits the Niger from Dendi.
1468: Sunni Ali takes Timbuktu from the Tuareg.
1475: the Inner Niger Delta and the northern Sahel pass to Songhai in Cliopatria.
1493: Askia Muhammad founds the Askiya dynasty.
Undated, under Askia Muhammad (1493-1528): 'the salt mines of Taghaza were brought within the empire's boundaries.'
1564: Cliopatria extends the shape west to the Senegal coast.
13 March 1591: the Moroccans meet the Songhai at Tondibi.
1591: the old empire dissolves into small kingdoms.
1591: the fighting for the Niger bend ends with the cities in Moroccan hands; the Tondibi page speaks of about a decade of sporadic fighting after, and gives no later date.
1591: the Askia court leaves Gao for Dendi.

wars.name: Sunni Ali's conquests on the Niger
wars.outcome: Songhai takes Mema (1460s), Timbuktu (1468) and Djenné (1475, after a siege laid in 1473), and the Inner Niger Delta.

wars.name: Songhai-Mossi wars
wars.outcome: Sunni Ali 'had to abandon this project ... to defeat an invasion by the Mossi people' in 1483.

wars.name: Battle of Anfao (Askia coup)
wars.outcome: Askia Muhammad (Ture) defeats Sonni Baru outside Gao in April 1493 and founds the Askiya dynasty; a change of dynasty, not of land.

wars.name: Askia Muhammad's campaigns
wars.outcome: Diafunu captured 1501; Borgu invaded 1504 'ended in disaster'; Walata captured but not held 1504; Futa Kingi destroyed and the Kingdom of Diarra brought under the empire's sway 1512 (no location on the page); another campaign against Agadez 1515.

wars.name: Songhai civil wars
wars.outcome: Askia Musa deposes his father in August 1528; 'several civil wars within the empire ensured the empire's continued decline', and a war of succession after Daoud (1582) 'split it into two feuding factions'.

wars.name: Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire
wars.outcome: Judar Pasha, sent by Ahmad al-Mansur (the lead has the force sent in 1590, the text 1591), crosses the Niger on 28 February 1591 and defeats Askia Ishaq II at Tondibi on 13 March; Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné are sacked.

wars.name: Songhai resistance in Dendi
wars.outcome: Nuh holds out at Lulami; Mahmud ibn Zarqun's two-year war ends with his withdrawal in 1594 and death that year; a later Moroccan campaign fails and Nuh's followers depose him in 1599.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Songhai frontier: the Niger valley cities are known, the Sahelian and Saharan limits (Taghaza, Aïr, the Senegal side) are approximate throughout.
